# The 2D Laplace suite {#sec-ds-laplace2d}

Heat a wavy metal plate from its edge and ask for the temperature
everywhere inside: that is this suite. It is the foundation of the
program's difficulty ladder — linear, scalar, exactly solvable — and
the place where every architectural claim must survive first contact,
because exact labels make every failure unambiguous.

## The problem

A star-shaped domain $\Omega$ with a smooth, randomly generated
boundary carries prescribed values $g$ (Dirichlet data) on its edge;
the model must produce the interior field at arbitrary query points.
The figure below shows one complete sample exactly as the model
receives it: boundary cells colored by their data, outward normals,
and bare query points — nothing else.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ds1-bc-diagram
#| fig-cap: >
#|   One training sample, as posed. The boundary polyline (colored by its
#|   Dirichlet value g) is the entire input: each cell carries its position,
#|   size, outward normal (gray arrows), BC type, and value. The interior
#|   query points (dots) carry nothing — they are bare coordinates at which
#|   the field is requested.
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import torch
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, Normalize

for _entry in (Path("..").resolve(), Path("..").resolve() / "problems"):
    if str(_entry) not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, str(_entry))
from conformal_laplace import (
    build_domain_sample,
    conformal_map,
    evaluate_potential,
    map_to_physical,
    sample_drive,
    sample_geometry,
)

INK, INK2 = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e"
DIVERGING = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "book_diverging", ["#2a78d6", "#f0efec", "#e34948"])


def make_sample(seed, *, geo_modes=(2, 3), deform=(0.05, 0.35),
                drive_modes=tuple(range(1, 9)), n_boundary=128, n_query=8):
    geometry = sample_geometry(seed, modes=geo_modes,
                               deformation_range=deform)
    drive = sample_drive(seed + 1000, modes=drive_modes)
    return build_domain_sample(geometry, drive, n_boundary=n_boundary,
                               n_query=n_query, query_seed=seed)


sample = make_sample(11, n_boundary=96, n_query=140)
boundary = sample.domain.boundaries["dirichlet"]
pts = boundary.points.numpy()
cells = boundary.cells.numpy()
trace = boundary.cell_data["boundary_value"].numpy()
queries = sample.domain.interior.points.numpy()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 5.2))
amp = np.abs(trace - trace.mean()).max()
norm = Normalize(trace.mean() - amp, trace.mean() + amp)
segs = pts[cells]
ax.add_collection(LineCollection(segs, colors=DIVERGING(norm(trace)),
                                 linewidths=3.4, capstyle="round", zorder=3))
centroids = segs.mean(axis=1)
normals = boundary.cell_normals.numpy()
stride = 4
ax.quiver(centroids[::stride, 0], centroids[::stride, 1],
          normals[::stride, 0], normals[::stride, 1],
          color="#898781", width=0.004, scale=18, zorder=2)
ax.plot(queries[:, 0], queries[:, 1], ".", color=INK, ms=3.5, zorder=1)
ax.annotate("Dirichlet boundary:\n$u = g$ (color)",
            xy=tuple(centroids[10]), xytext=(0.02, 0.97),
            textcoords="axes fraction", fontsize=10, color=INK, va="top",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=INK2, lw=0.9))
ax.annotate("query points:\ncoordinates only", xy=tuple(queries[30]),
            xytext=(0.70, 0.04), textcoords="axes fraction", fontsize=10,
            color=INK, arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=INK2, lw=0.9))
sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm)
fig.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, shrink=0.75, label="boundary data $g$")
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.grid(False)
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

In symbols: the governing problem is

$$
\Delta u = 0 \ \text{in } \Omega,
\qquad u = g \ \text{on } \partial\Omega ,
$$

and every label is **exact**: domains are conformal images of the unit
disk under random Laurent-mode maps, drives are harmonic compositions
in the disk frame, so the interior solution is available in closed form
at any point — no solver in the loop, no numerical error to hide behind
(@sec-part-eval). The declared contracts: **similarity equivariance**
(always, via the intrinsic gauge) and **drive-linearity** — Laplace is
linear, so `field_mode="linear"` makes superposition structural, exact
to floating point for any weights.

## Why this rung

Every claim in this book starts here for three reasons. *Exactness*:
contract violations and accuracy failures are unambiguous at the
$10^{-14}$ level. *Analytic oracles*: the true solution operator is
available, so "how far from perfect" is measured, not estimated. And
*control*: geometry, drive frequency, and discretization vary
independently, which is what makes the one-question-per-split
evaluation of @sec-part-eval possible at all.

Its **hard-geometry extension** — the multi-body and deep-cavity
families below — keeps the same exact physics while making the
*geometry* the hard part: fields that pairwise invariants alone
provably cannot resolve, which is where boundary self-attention earns
its keep (@sec-mixed-bc, @sec-encoder-stress).

## The gallery

Twelve training-family samples, drawn exactly as the training
distribution draws them. Each panel is the exact interior field; the
boundary ring is the input data.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ds1-gallery
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Training-family samples: exact interior fields u on conformal-star
#|   domains, boundary colored by its Dirichlet data. Colors normalize per
#|   sample about the boundary mean, so the geometry distribution and the
#|   field structure read together.


def conformal_panel(ax, seed, *, geo_modes=(2, 3), deform=(0.05, 0.35),
                    drive_modes=tuple(range(1, 9)), title=None,
                    n_ring=200, n_rad=60):
    s = make_sample(seed, geo_modes=geo_modes, deform=deform,
                    drive_modes=drive_modes)
    radii = torch.linspace(0.0, 0.995, n_rad, dtype=torch.float64)[None, :]
    angles = torch.linspace(0.0, 2 * np.pi, n_ring,
                            dtype=torch.float64)[:, None]
    disk = (radii * torch.exp(1j * angles)).to(torch.complex128)
    physical = map_to_physical(s.geometry, disk, s.similarity).numpy()
    field = evaluate_potential(s.drive, disk).numpy()
    b = s.domain.boundaries["dirichlet"]
    tr = b.cell_data["boundary_value"].numpy()
    vmid = float(tr.mean())
    amp = max(np.abs(field - vmid).max(), np.abs(tr - vmid).max())
    ax.contourf(physical[..., 0], physical[..., 1], field,
                levels=np.linspace(vmid - amp, vmid + amp, 25),
                cmap=DIVERGING)
    segs2 = b.points[b.cells].numpy()
    ax.add_collection(LineCollection(
        segs2, colors=DIVERGING(Normalize(vmid - amp, vmid + amp)(tr)),
        linewidths=2.0, capstyle="round"))
    bp = b.points.numpy()
    lo, hi = bp.min(axis=0), bp.max(axis=0)
    mid2, half2 = (lo + hi) / 2, (hi - lo).max() / 2 * 1.06
    ax.set_xlim(mid2[0] - half2, mid2[0] + half2)
    ax.set_ylim(mid2[1] - half2, mid2[1] + half2)
    ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.grid(False)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)
    if title is not None:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=8.5, color=INK)


fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 4, figsize=(9.4, 7.2))
for ax, seed in zip(axes.ravel(),
                    (3, 7, 11, 17, 23, 29, 31, 37, 41, 47, 53, 59)):
    conformal_panel(ax, seed, title=f"seed {seed}")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### The three OOD axes, illustrated

Evaluation never mixes questions: each split moves **one** axis away
from training (@sec-part-eval). The rows below make the axes visible on
matched seeds by moving the generator dials directly — geometry modes
the training family never uses, stronger deformation of familiar modes,
and drive frequencies beyond the training band.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ds1-splits
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The OOD axes, one per row, on matched seeds. Row 1: the training
#|   family (Laurent modes {2,3}, deformation 0.05-0.35, drive modes 1-8).
#|   Row 2: unseen geometry modes {5,7}. Row 3: stronger deformation
#|   (0.35-0.55) of the training modes. Row 4: unseen drive frequencies
#|   (modes 9-14) on training-family geometry. The frozen evaluation banks
#|   implement these axes with their exact protocols (@sec-part-eval);
#|   these panels vary the same dials illustratively.
rows = [
    ("training family", dict()),
    ("unseen geometry modes", dict(geo_modes=(5, 7))),
    ("stronger deformation", dict(deform=(0.35, 0.55))),
    ("unseen drive frequencies", dict(drive_modes=tuple(range(9, 15)))),
]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 3, figsize=(7.6, 10.0))
for row, (label, dials) in enumerate(rows):
    for col, seed in enumerate((5, 13, 19)):
        conformal_panel(axes[row, col], seed,
                        title=label if col == 1 else None, **dials)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### The hard-geometry families

The same exact physics on geometry built to defeat pairwise reasoning:
multiple bodies whose separating gaps carry the field structure, and
deep cavities whose openings hide it.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ds1-stress
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Hard-geometry samples: multi-body (left pair, narrow-gap dial shown)
#|   and deep-cavity (right pair, deep-slot dial shown). Exact fields on
#|   masked grids; excluded bodies read as solid gray; x marks are the
#|   charges generating the exact solutions — label machinery, never model
#|   input.
import matplotlib.patheffects as mpe

from encoder_stress import (
    SPLITS,
    _in_domain,
    build_deep_cavity_sample,
    build_multi_body_sample,
    harmonic_potential,
)


def stress_panel(ax, s, n_grid=150):
    b = s.domain.boundaries["dirichlet"]
    p = b.points.numpy()
    lo, hi = p.min(axis=0), p.max(axis=0)
    mid, half = (lo + hi) / 2, (hi - lo).max() / 2 * 1.05
    xs = np.linspace(mid[0] - half, mid[0] + half, n_grid)
    ys = np.linspace(mid[1] - half, mid[1] + half, n_grid)
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    grid_points = torch.tensor(np.stack([X.ravel(), Y.ravel()], axis=1))
    inside = torch.cat([
        _in_domain(s.boundary_loops, grid_points[i:i + 8192])
        for i in range(0, grid_points.shape[0], 8192)
    ]).numpy()
    values = harmonic_potential(
        grid_points, s.charge_positions, s.charge_strengths).numpy()
    field = np.ma.array(values.reshape(n_grid, n_grid),
                        mask=~inside.reshape(n_grid, n_grid))
    tr = b.cell_data["boundary_value"].numpy()
    vmid = float(tr.mean())
    amp = max(float(np.abs(field - vmid).max()),
              float(np.abs(tr - vmid).max()))
    norm2 = Normalize(vmid - amp, vmid + amp)
    ax.contourf(X, Y, field, levels=np.linspace(vmid - amp, vmid + amp, 25),
                cmap=DIVERGING, alpha=0.85)
    for hole in s.boundary_loops[1:]:
        ax.fill(hole[:, 0].numpy(), hole[:, 1].numpy(),
                facecolor="#eae8e1", edgecolor="none", zorder=2)
    segs3 = b.points[b.cells].numpy()
    line = LineCollection(segs3, colors=DIVERGING(norm2(tr)),
                          linewidths=2.0, zorder=4, capstyle="round")
    line.set_path_effects(
        [mpe.Stroke(linewidth=2.7, foreground=INK), mpe.Normal()])
    ax.add_collection(line)
    charges = s.charge_positions.numpy()
    keep = (np.abs(charges[:, 0] - mid[0]) < 0.95 * half) & (
        np.abs(charges[:, 1] - mid[1]) < 0.95 * half)
    ax.plot(charges[keep, 0], charges[keep, 1], "x", color=INK, ms=4,
            mew=1.2, zorder=5)
    ax.set_xlim(mid[0] - half, mid[0] + half)
    ax.set_ylim(mid[1] - half, mid[1] + half)
    ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.grid(False)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)


fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(9.4, 2.8))
panels = [
    (build_multi_body_sample(3, **SPLITS["multi_body"]["in_distribution"]),
     "multi-body: in-distribution"),
    (build_multi_body_sample(7, **SPLITS["multi_body"]["narrow_gap"]),
     "multi-body: narrow gap"),
    (build_deep_cavity_sample(3, **SPLITS["deep_cavity"]["in_distribution"]),
     "deep cavity: in-distribution"),
    (build_deep_cavity_sample(9, **SPLITS["deep_cavity"]["deep_slot"]),
     "deep cavity: deep slot"),
]
for ax, (s, label) in zip(axes, panels):
    stress_panel(ax, s)
    ax.set_title(label, fontsize=8.5)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## The full evidence: encoder-stress families

Moved from the benchmarks chapter: the multi-body and deep-cavity studies.

### The encoder-stress suites: geometry that pair invariants cannot see {#sec-encoder-stress}

These suites (`encoder_stress.py`; their place in the agenda is
@sec-future) exist to test a claim no earlier benchmark could
touch. Every prior 2D suite lives on a (deformed) disk,
where two boundary points close in $\mathbb R^2$ are also close along the
boundary — so a kernel of *pairwise Euclidean invariants* never has to
see around geometry, and the attention encoder's claim to existence
(global boundary-to-boundary information flow before the query decode)
goes untested. Two families close the gap, both with
exterior-point-charge exact labels
($u = \sum_j q_j \log\|x - c_j\|$, charges strictly outside the domain
closure) and unit-RMS boundary traces:

- **Multi-body**: the interior of a circle minus two disjoint disks —
  multiply connected, three Dirichlet boundaries merged into a single
  boundary mesh (identity conveyed geometrically). Some in-disk charges
  are deliberately biased toward the gap-facing surface of their disk,
  so in the narrow-gap regime the trace on the near face of one body is
  dominated by a charge hidden inside the *other* — genuine inter-body
  coupling. The difficulty dial is the surface gap over the sum of disk
  radii; splits: in-distribution, narrow-gap, single-body, and
  unseen-charge-count.
- **Deep cavity**: a simply connected domain whose boundary is a disk
  with a deep, narrow, smoothly filleted slot (a "C-shape"), charges
  nestled *inside the slot* — outside the domain but deep in the cavity
  — so two interior points on opposite cavity walls are Euclidean-close
  while the field between them is mediated by the whole cavity
  geometry. The dial is slot depth over width; splits: in-distribution,
  deep-slot, and a convex control.

```{python}
#| label: fig-stress-multibody
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The multi-body family, one exact case per split, rendered live from
#|   the generator: interior field translucent inside the boundary,
#|   boundary trace emphasized on top (colors per sample, diverging
#|   about the boundary mean). Crosses are the generator's logarithmic
#|   point charges -- exterior to the domain (inside the excluded bodies
#|   or beyond the outer circle), private label-generation state no
#|   model ever sees; exterior charges beyond the crop are not shown. In
#|   the narrow-gap case the hot spot on the near face of each body is
#|   produced by a charge hidden inside the other body -- the inter-body
#|   coupling that pair invariants cannot see.
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.patheffects as mpe
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import torch
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, Normalize

for _entry in (Path("..").resolve(), Path("..").resolve() / "problems"):
    if str(_entry) not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, str(_entry))
from encoder_stress import (
    SPLITS,
    _in_domain,
    build_deep_cavity_sample,
    build_multi_body_sample,
    harmonic_potential,
)

INK, INK2 = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e"
DIVERGING = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "book_diverging", ["#2a78d6", "#f0efec", "#e34948"])


def stress_panel(ax, sample, n_grid=170):
    """Exact interior field on a masked grid, using the generator's own
    domain-membership predicate (winding numbers), chunked for memory."""
    boundary = sample.domain.boundaries["dirichlet"]
    pts = boundary.points.numpy()
    lo, hi = pts.min(axis=0), pts.max(axis=0)
    mid, half = (lo + hi) / 2, (hi - lo).max() / 2 * 1.05
    xs = np.linspace(mid[0] - half, mid[0] + half, n_grid)
    ys = np.linspace(mid[1] - half, mid[1] + half, n_grid)
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    grid_points = torch.tensor(np.stack([X.ravel(), Y.ravel()], axis=1))
    inside = torch.cat([
        _in_domain(sample.boundary_loops, grid_points[i : i + 8192])
        for i in range(0, grid_points.shape[0], 8192)
    ]).numpy()
    values = harmonic_potential(
        grid_points, sample.charge_positions, sample.charge_strengths).numpy()
    field = np.ma.array(values.reshape(n_grid, n_grid),
                        mask=~inside.reshape(n_grid, n_grid))

    trace = boundary.cell_data["boundary_value"].numpy()
    vmid = float(trace.mean())
    amp = max(float(np.abs(field - vmid).max()), float(np.abs(trace - vmid).max()))
    norm = Normalize(vmid - amp, vmid + amp)

    cs = ax.contourf(X, Y, field, levels=np.linspace(vmid - amp, vmid + amp, 27),
                     cmap=DIVERGING, alpha=0.82)
    cs.set_edgecolor("face")
    for hole in sample.boundary_loops[1:]:  # excluded bodies read as solid
        ax.fill(hole[:, 0].numpy(), hole[:, 1].numpy(),
                facecolor="#eae8e1", edgecolor="none", zorder=2)
    segments = boundary.points[boundary.cells].numpy()
    boundary_line = LineCollection(
        segments, colors=DIVERGING(norm(trace)), linewidths=2.2,
        zorder=4, capstyle="round")
    boundary_line.set_path_effects(
        [mpe.Stroke(linewidth=3.0, foreground=INK), mpe.Normal()])
    ax.add_collection(boundary_line)
    charges = sample.charge_positions.numpy()
    keep = (np.abs(charges[:, 0] - mid[0]) < 0.93 * half) & (
        np.abs(charges[:, 1] - mid[1]) < 0.93 * half)
    ax.plot(charges[keep, 0], charges[keep, 1], "x", color=INK, ms=5,
            mew=1.4, zorder=5)
    ax.set_xlim(mid[0] - half, mid[0] + half)
    ax.set_ylim(mid[1] - half, mid[1] + half)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.grid(False)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)


def stress_colorbar(fig, position):
    cax = fig.add_axes(position)
    sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(cmap=DIVERGING, norm=Normalize(-1, 1))
    cbar = fig.colorbar(sm, cax=cax)
    cbar.set_ticks([-1, 0, 1])
    cbar.set_ticklabels(["min", "boundary\nmean", "max"], fontsize=8)
    cbar.set_label("potential $u$ (per sample)", fontsize=9)


cases = [
    ("in_distribution", 3, "in-distribution"),
    ("narrow_gap", 7, "narrow gap"),
    ("single_body", 11, "single body"),
    ("unseen_charge_count", 5, "unseen charge count"),
]
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(9.2, 2.9))
grid = fig.add_gridspec(1, 4, left=0.02, right=0.86, top=0.90, bottom=0.04,
                        wspace=0.06)
for col, (split, seed, label) in enumerate(cases):
    sample = build_multi_body_sample(seed, **SPLITS["multi_body"][split])
    ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, col])
    stress_panel(ax, sample)
    ax.set_title(label, fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
    if not math.isnan(sample.geometry.gap_ratio):
        ax.text(0.5, -0.03, f"gap ratio {sample.geometry.gap_ratio:.2f}",
                transform=ax.transAxes, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=8,
                color=INK2)
stress_colorbar(fig, [0.89, 0.20, 0.018, 0.60])
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-stress-cavity
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The deep-cavity family, same rendering conventions as the
#|   multi-body gallery. Charges (crosses) nestled inside the slot are
#|   outside the domain but deep in the cavity, so opposite slot walls
#|   are Euclidean-close while the exact field between them -- the plume
#|   filling the slot -- is mediated by the whole cavity geometry. The
#|   difficulty dial is slot depth over width; the convex control
#|   (right) is the same generator at zero slot depth.
# Reuses stress_panel/stress_colorbar from the multi-body cell above
# (same kernel session).
cases = [
    ("in_distribution", 3, "in-distribution"),
    ("deep_slot", 7, "deep slot"),
    ("convex_control", 11, "convex control"),
]
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7.2, 2.9))
grid = fig.add_gridspec(1, 3, left=0.02, right=0.84, top=0.90, bottom=0.04,
                        wspace=0.06)
for col, (split, seed, label) in enumerate(cases):
    sample = build_deep_cavity_sample(seed, **SPLITS["deep_cavity"][split])
    ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, col])
    stress_panel(ax, sample, n_grid=200)
    ax.set_title(label, fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
    g = sample.geometry
    if g.slot_depth > 0:
        ax.text(0.5, -0.03,
                f"depth/width {g.slot_depth / (2 * g.slot_half_width):.1f}",
                transform=ax.transAxes, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=8,
                color=INK2)
stress_colorbar(fig, [0.875, 0.20, 0.022, 0.60])
plt.show()
```

Every generated sample is **certified at build time**: cell-orientation
winding numbers place all queries inside and all charges outside, charge
standoff from the discretized boundary is checked numerically, the
cavity curve passes an exact all-pairs segment-intersection test, and
the multi-body boundaries are verified disjoint. The **free-form pair
kernel is the load-bearing control**: it is exactly the model class that
sees only pair invariants, so any split where it fails and an
encoder-bearing model succeeds is direct evidence for global boundary
coupling. One honest caveat from the suite's validation: the families
are a *separation dial*, not a binary proof — the construction makes
pair invariants blind to the coupling, but how much that blindness
costs is an empirical question the control answers, not a theorem.
